answer: In a coastal haven where AI agents route cargo through an inlet beneath a rocky ledge, each agent must lock a deposit before bidding for delivery jobs. A contract slashes that deposit if anyone submits two conflicting job commitments signed by the same agent for the same slot. Creating more identities buys no free capacity: each needs its own deposit, so a thousand fake bidders require a thousand deposits, tying up capital and risking losses when they cheat.
